mechaber.he:
איסור עריות בגרים ודינן לענין עדות וחליצה. ובו י"א סעיפים:
דין תורה שמותר לגר שישא אמו או אחותו מאמו שנתגיירו אבל חכמים אסרו דבר זה כדי שלא יאמרו באנו מקדושה חמורה לקדושה קלה וכן גר שבא על אמו או אחותו והיא בגיותה הרי זה כבא על ארמית:
mechaber.en:
Prohibition of forbidden relations with converts and their law regarding testimony and chalitzah. And it contains 11 seifim.
By Torah law it is permitted for a convert to marry his mother or his maternal sister who converted; but the Sages forbade this matter so they should not say, "We came from a severe sanctity to a light sanctity"; and likewise a convert who had relations with his mother or sister while she was still a gentile — behold it is like one who had relations with a gentile woman.

siftei_kohen.he: דין תורה כו'. כלומר דדין תורה מותר לגר לישא אמו או אחותו מאמו וכל שכן מאביו דגר שנתגייר כקטן שנולד דמי אלא שחכמים אסרו בשאר האם כיון דגם בני נח אסורים בשאר האם כדי שלא יאמרו באנו מקדושה חמורה לקדושה קלה ח"ו אבל בשאר האב לא גזרו כדלקמן ס"ז דאין אבות לעובד כוכבים זהו דעת הרמב"ם והמחבר:
siftei_kohen.en: By Torah law, etc. Meaning, by Torah law a convert may marry his mother or his maternal sister, and certainly a paternal relative, because a convert who converted is regarded as a newborn child. The Sages, however, prohibited maternal relatives, since descendants of Noah are also forbidden to maternal relatives, so that people should not say, Heaven forbid, that they have passed from a more stringent sanctity to a more lenient sanctity. They did not decree regarding paternal relatives, as stated below in seif 7, because a non-Jew has no legally recognized paternity. This is the view of the Rambam and the Mechaber.

baer_heitev.he: מאמו. כתב הש"ך וכ"ש מאביו דגר שנתגייר כקטן שנולד דמי אלא שחכמים גזרו וכ' והיינו בשאר האם אבל בשאר האב לא גזרו דאין אבות לעובדי כוכבים עכ"ל:
baer_heitev.en: From his mother. Siftei Kohen writes: All the more so from his father, for a convert who converted is considered like a newborn child; the prohibition exists only because of a rabbinic decree. This applies to maternal relatives. The Sages did not decree concerning paternal relatives, for legal paternity is not recognized among non-Jews. These are his words.

beer_hagolah.he: לשון הרמב"ם פי"ד מהלכות אישות מהא דאמר רבא לרב נחמן חזי מר וכו' יבמות דף כ"ב ע"א וכאיכא דאמרי דפליג רב אחא בר יעקב אפילו באחין מן האם שם דף צ"ז ע"ב:
beer_hagolah.en: The wording of Rambam, chapter 14 of Hilchot Issurei Biah, from Rava's statement to Rav Nachman, Yevamot 22a, and according to the version that Rav Acha bar Yaakov disagrees even regarding maternal brothers, Yevamot 97b.

beur_hagra.he:
דין תורה כו'. יבמות כ"ב א' השתא ומה ערוה כו' ושם ומ"ש מעריות כו' וגר כו':
כדי שלא כו'. שם ועתוס' שם ד"ה ערוה כו' אבל הרמב"ם לא ס"ל כדבריהם דס"ל דמן האב מותר כמ"ש בס"ב וס"ג. כ"מ ע"ש. וליתא דגם להרמב"ם צ"ל כדברי תוס' דהא אחות אם ואשת אחיו מן האם מותר בעובד כוכבים ואסור לגר וע"כ משום אחלופי אלא דלדידיה אמו ואחותו מאמו הוא משום שמא יאמרו ואחות אם ואשת אחיו מאם משום אחלופי וכאן לא נקט אלא אותן שהיו אסורות בנכריותו ונ"מ דאלו אפי' בדיעבד יוציא אבל הנך א"צ וכמ"ש בס"ב ועמש"ש:
beur_hagra.en:
The law of the Torah, etc. Yevamos 22a: “Now, if with regard to forbidden relations,” etc.; and there, “And what is different about forbidden relations,” etc.; “and a convert,” etc.
How so, etc. Rambam writes in chapter 9 of Hilchos Melachim that six forbidden relations apply to Bnei Noach: his mother, his father's wife, a married woman, his maternal sister, a male, and an animal. This is derived from the verse, “Therefore a man shall leave his father,” meaning his father's wife; “and his mother,” literally; “and cleave,” but not to a male; “to his wife,” but not to another man's wife; “and they shall become one flesh,” excluding an animal. Scripture also states, “She is indeed my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother, and she became my wife.” These are Rabbi Akiva's words in Sanhedrin 58a. Yet according to Rabbi Akiva one's sister is permitted, as explained there on 58b. See Rashi there, s.v. “Come and hear,” and also, etc. Rather, Rambam ruled in accordance with the Sages on 57b. A baraisa supports Rabbi Yochanan: “Every forbidden relation,” etc.; and the Sages say, “Many,” etc. It appears that the word “many” should not be read there. Rather, the text means: there are offenses for which a Jewish beit din, etc. This is the case explained at the end of the baraisa, “If he came,” etc. The only such cases are his sister and a betrothed maiden. The reference to a betrothed maiden requires study. The prohibition of his sister is derived from “Therefore a man shall leave,” etc. Rabbi Akiva must interpret that verse with difficulty, whereas the Sages explain it according to its plain meaning. Toras Kohanim on Parashas Kedoshim states concerning “A man,” etc., “It is a kindness.” Lest you say that Kayin married his sister, Scripture states, “It is a kindness,” teaching that the world at its beginning could be built only through kindness. This accords with Sanhedrin 58b: “Come and hear: Why,” etc., and not with the Gemara's rejection there, and not with Rashi's explanation on 57b, s.v. “Many,” etc. Ramban likewise writes this, except that he maintains that all maternal relatives are forbidden according to the Sages. The only difference between Ramban and Rambam is a mother's maternal sister, as Ramban explains. There are twenty two forbidden relations. Four are not based on kinship: a male, an animal, a married woman, and a niddah. All are forbidden to a non-Jew except niddah, whose prohibition does not apply to them. Eighteen are based on kinship, as stated at the beginning of Yevamos: fifteen women, etc., and six forbidden relations, etc., totaling twenty one together with the other categories. A brother's wife is counted there three times: a paternal brother's wife, a maternal brother's wife, and the wife of a brother who was not yet born. A sister is counted twice, a paternal sister and a maternal sister. Seven relations are therefore one's own relatives, seven come through one's wife, and four are wives of relatives whom the husband makes forbidden to his wife. For Bnei Noach, all seven relations arising through one's wife are permitted, because marriage does not create this network of kinship for a non-Jew. Likewise, the four wives of relatives are all permitted, except a father's wife, which Rabbi Akiva derives from Scripture. According to Rabbi Eliezer, even those are permitted. Of the seven personal relatives, all paternal relatives are permitted, as stated in chapter 11 of Yevamos, 98a, because a non-Jew has no halachic father. Therefore, Sanhedrin 58b states that a non-Jew is permitted to his daughter, and certainly to his granddaughter through either a son or daughter. Rabbi Akiva likewise permits a father's sister for this reason, although Rabbi Eliezer includes her through a Scriptural derivation. Ramban maintains that even Rabbi Akiva prohibits a mother's sister. He writes that the word “saying” includes all maternal relatives. Rambam, however, maintains that even according to the Sages no maternal relatives are forbidden beyond one's mother and maternal sister, who are explicitly stated. This is parallel to Rabbi Meir's understanding of Rabbi Akiva. Rabbi Meir and the Sages disagree only about one's sister and about the interpretation of the verse, as the Gemara cited above explains. Sanhedrin 57b asks, “Does Rabbi Meir maintain that every,” etc. Ramban explains that the question addresses only the latter clause, which states that a ben Noach is not warned, etc., whereas here the baraisa teaches that his sister, etc. The Gemara does not question the father's wife, because the Sages did not decree other paternal relations upon converts. This differs from Rashi there, s.v. “And some teach,” etc. Proof is that the Gemara challenges specifically according to Rabbi Meir. According to Rashi's explanation, the same difficulty would apply to the Sages, who do not disagree about this point. The Gemara answers: “This is not difficult; this is Rabbi Meir,” etc. The baraisa therefore also does not follow the Sages, who disagree only regarding his sister, because they necessarily agree with Rabbi Akiva, as is evident from their conceding to Rabbi Meir concerning offenses punishable by a Jewish court. In the dispute between Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov and Rabbi Shimon in Yevamos 97b, Rambam rules like Rav Acha bar Yaakov and the first version, unlike Rif. His reason is the statement on 98a: Rava said, “That which the Sages said,” etc., which implies that even rabbinically a convert has no paternal relationship. The Gemara continues that two twin brothers, etc. Accordingly, every relationship containing a paternal element is permitted initially: a father's maternal sister, a mother's paternal sister, and a paternal sister. Although the baraisa there prohibits all of them, it was already explained as following Rabbi Eliezer, who maintains that a father's sister is forbidden to a ben Noach. According to Rabbi Akiva and the Sages, every relationship containing a paternal element is completely permitted. Ramban and Rashba likewise write this. A mother's maternal sister, however, is rabbinically forbidden to a convert although permitted to a ben Noach. The statement that a non-Jew has no father implies that maternal kinship does exist. Maternal brothers are likewise forbidden, as explained above. Paternal kinship created through marriage is permitted, even a father's wife, according to all opinions, except for the wife of a maternal brother, as explained above. This follows the same rule as one's own relatives. The Gemara's exchange, “What, is it not,” etc.; “No,” etc., concerns only a brother's wife. It does not support Raavad's explanation that it concerns every prohibition arising through marriage, for the Gemara also lists the wife of a father's brother, who is certainly permitted even if she married him after he became a convert. This is Ramban's explanation. There is a further distinction between the baraisa and the Sages. According to the baraisa, one who married his mother's maternal sister must divorce her. According to the Sages, he may remain married to her, just as Rabbi Meir permits one to remain married to his father's paternal sister, since the prohibition is only because of possible confusion. The same applies to a mother's maternal sister according to Rabbi Akiva and the Sages, and certainly to the wife of a maternal brother. This is Rambam's approach. Accordingly, his words, “If he was married,” etc., refer to the other relatives, etc. (Collected note) See what I wrote there. Rambam's general rule is as follows. For a ben Noach, his mother, maternal sister, and father's wife are forbidden, while all other relatives are fully permitted, in accordance with the Sages who disagree with Rabbi Meir. For a convert, every paternal relationship is completely permitted, whether it is his own blood relationship or one created through marriage. He may therefore marry even his father's wife, and in this respect his status is more lenient than that of a non-Jew. Conversely, every maternal relationship is forbidden to him, whether personal or created through marriage. Thus, among his own relatives, his mother and his mother's maternal sister are forbidden. Through his wife, his wife's maternal sister, his wife's daughter, her daughter's daughter, his mother-in-law, and his mother-in-law's mother are forbidden, as stated in seif 5 concerning one who marries, etc.; “the same applies,” etc. The same rule applies to these relations, as Tosafos and Ramban write. Through marriage, the wife of his maternal brother is also forbidden. These total nine forbidden relations. Ramban's approach regarding a convert agrees with Rambam, but regarding a non-Jew he writes that according to all opinions every maternal relation is forbidden, every paternal relation is permitted, and ordinary marital kinship creates no prohibition. The only exceptions are those specifically enumerated: a father's maternal sister according to Rabbi Eliezer, and a father's wife according to Rabbi Akiva. Rabbi Meir, according to Rabbi Akiva, prohibits only maternal relatives whose violation is punishable by a Jewish court, whereas Rabbi Eliezer and the Sages include even relations punishable by kares. Rashi follows another approach. See Ramban's discussion. (End of collected note.)

rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.he: (סי' רס"ט סעיף י"א) פסול לדון את ישראל. כתב הרמב"ם (פ"ד מהל' מלכים ה"ד) אין מעמידים מלך מקהל גרים עד שתהיה אמו מישראל ולא למלכות בלבד אלא לכל שררות שבישראל וכו' ואפי' ממונה על אמת המים שמחלקים ממנו לשדות ואצ"ל דיין או נשיא וכו' אפי' אחר כמה דורות. הועתק במהריק"ש וע' ?בהג"מ:
rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.en: (Siman 269 seif 11) Disqualified to judge Israel. Rambam wrote (chapter 4 of Hilchot Melachim halachah 4): We do not appoint a king from the congregation of converts until his mother is from Israel; and not only for kingship but for any authority in Israel, etc.; and even one appointed over the water distribution that they divide from it to the fields — and all the more so a judge or nasi, etc., even after many generations. Copied in Maharikash — see Hagahot Maimoniyot.

mechaber.he: כיצד דין גרים בעריות של שאר בשר אם היה נשוי כשהוא עובד כוכבים לאמו או לאחותו מאמו ונתגיירו מפרישין אותם ואם היה נשוי לשאר עריות ונתגייר הוא ואשתו אין מפרישין אותם:
mechaber.en: How is the law of converts regarding other forbidden relations? If he was married while a gentile to his mother or to his maternal sister and they converted — they separate them; and if he was married to other forbidden relations and he and his wife converted — they do not separate them.

siftei_kohen.he: בעריות של שאר בשר כו'. כלומר כך הוא דין גרים אם עבר על דתו בעוד שהוא עובד כוכבים ונשא אמו או אחותו מאמו ונתגיירו מפרישין אותן עולמית שאם לא ימחו בידו אע"פ שעבר בגיותו על דתו מ"מ יאמרו באנו מקדושה חמורה כו' שכבר עשיתי באיסור ועכשיו הותרה לי ואם היה נשוי שאר עריות בגיותו אפי' מצד האם ונתגייר הוא ואשתו עמו כיון שאין האיסור אלא משום גזירה דישראל דלא ליתי לאחלופי כו' הואיל וכבר נשוי הוא אין מפרישין אותם עולמית רק ג' חדשים להבחין בין זרע שנזרע בקדושה לזרע שנזרע שלא בקדושה כדלקמן סעיף ט':
siftei_kohen.en: With regard to forbidden relations involving blood relatives, etc. Meaning, this is the law governing converts: If, while still a non-Jew, he violated the law binding upon him and married his mother or his maternal sister, and they then converted, they are separated permanently. Were beit din not to protest, although he had violated his law while a non-Jew, he would nevertheless say, 'We have passed from a more stringent sanctity, etc., for previously I acted while it was forbidden and now it has become permitted to me.' If he had married another forbidden relative while a non-Jew, even a maternal relative, and he and his wife converted together, since the prohibition is only because of the rabbinic decree applicable to Jews, lest confusion result, and he was already married to her, they are not separated permanently. They are separated only for three months, to distinguish between seed conceived in sanctity and seed conceived outside sanctity, as stated below in seif 9.

baer_heitev.he: אין. ומ"מ מפרישין אותן שלשה חדשים משום הבחנה כדלקמן ס"ט:
baer_heitev.en: There is no, etc. Nevertheless, they are separated for three months so that the child's parentage can be distinguished, as stated below in se'if 9.

beer_hagolah.he: שם וכרב ששת שם ולחומרא וכלישנא קמא וכר"ע שם דף צ"ח ע"א והא דאמר שם בדף כ"ב ע"א ומה ערוה גופה אי לאו שלא יאמרו וכו' על קרובי' שמצד האם דוקא קאמר וכמו שפי' הכ"מ שם והב"י וכן דעת הרי"ף:
beer_hagolah.en: There, following Rav Sheshet and stringently, according to the first version and Rabbi Akiva, Yevamot 98a. The statement on 22a concerning prohibited relationships refers specifically to maternal relatives, as Kesef Mishneh and Beit Yosef explain, and this is also the Rif's view.

beur_hagra.he:
כיצד כו'. הנה בפ"ט מה' מלכים כתב שש עריות אסורות על ב"נ האם ואשת אב ואשת איש ואחותו מאמו וזכור ובהמה שנאמר על כן יעזב איש את אביו זו אשת אביו ואת אמו כמשמעה ודבק ולא בזכור (כצ"ל ברמב"ם שם) באשתו ולא באשת חבירו והיו לבשר כו' להוציא בהמה כו' ונאמר אחותי בת אבי אך לא בת אמי ותהי לי לאשה. והוא דברי ר"ע בסנהדרין נ"ה א' אך אחותו לר"ע שרי כמש"ש ב' וערש"י שם ד"ה ת"ש וגם כו' אלא שהוא פסק כרבנן שם נ"ז ב' ת"כ דר"י כל ערוה כו' וחכ"א הרבה כו' ונראה דל"ג הרבה אלא יש שאין ב"ד של ישראל כו' והיינו ההיא דמפרש בסיפא בא כו' והן אחותו לבד ונערה המאורסה (צ"ע מהו בנערה המאורסה) אחותו מקרא דע"כ יעזב כו' דלר"ע צריך לדחוקי ורבנן מוקי כפשטיה ובת"כ פ' קדושים ואיש כו' חסד הוא ושמא תאמר קין נשא אחותו ת"ל חסד הוא ועולם מתחלתו לא נברא אלא בחסד וכמש"ש נ"ה ב' ת"ש מפני מה כו' ולא כדיחוייא דהתם ודלא כפירש"י שם נ"ז ב' ד"ה הרבה כו' וכ"כ הרמב"ן אלא שכתב דכל אותן שמאם אסורות לרבנן ואין בינו לבין הרמב"ם אלא אחות האם מן האם וכמ"ש ברמב"ן. דכ"ב עריות הן ד' שאינן מצד קורבה זכר ובהמה ואשת איש ונדה וכולן אסורות לעובד כוכבים חוץ נדה דלית להו וח"י עריות מצד קורבה כמ"ש בפ"א דיבמות ט"ו נשים כו' שש עריות כו' הרי כ"א ואשת אחיו חשיב שם ג' פעמים מאביו ומאמו ושלא היה בעולמו ואחותו ב"פ מאביו ומאמו והנה שבע הן קורבת עצמו ושבע מצד אשתו וד' אשת קרובים שבעל אוסר על אשתו והנה בב"נ שבע שמצד אשתו כולן מותרים דאין אישות לעובר כוכבים וכן ד' של אשת קרובים כולן מותרים לבד אשת אביו דאתרבאי מקרא לר"ע אבל לר"א כולן מותרים וז' שמצד עצמו אותן שמצד אב כולן מותרים כמ"ש ביבמות פי"א (צ"ח א') דאין אב לעובד כוכבים לכן אמרו שם נ"ח ב' דעובד כוכבים מותר בבתו וכ"ש בבת בתו ובת בנו וכן אחות האב לר"ע מה"ט אלא לר"א אתרבאי מקרא אבל אחות האם ס"ל לרמב"ן דאסור אף לר"ע וכתב משום דכתיב לאמר אתרבאי כל שמצד אם אבל הרמב"ם ס"ל דאינן אסורין אף לרבנן אלא אמו ואחותו שמפורשין וכמו לר"מ אליבא דר"ע ול"פ ר"מ וחכמים אלא באחותו ובפי' דקרא כמ"ש בגמ' הנ"ל ופריך שם נ"ז ב' וסבר ר"מ כל כו' ופי' הרמב"ן דקושיא לא קאי אלא אסיפא דמילתא דאמר אין ב"נ מוזהר כו' וכאן תני אחותו כו' אבל מאשת אביו לא פריך דלא גזרו שאר אב בגרים דלא כפירש"י שם ד"ה ואיכא דתני כו' וראיה ממה דפריך לר"מ דוקא ואי כפירש"י גם לרבנן קשה דהא רבנן ל"פ בזה ומשני ל"ק הא ר"מ כו' וה"ה דלא אתי הברייתא כרבנן דל"פ אלא באחותו דהא ע"כ כר"ע ס"ל מדמודי בחייבי מיתות ב"ד לר"מ ובפלוגתא דראב"י ור"ש ביבמות צ"ז ב' פסק כרב אחא בר יעקב וכלישנא קמא דלא כרי"ף וטעמו ממש"ש צ"ח א' אמר רבא הא דאמור רבנן כו' משמע דאף מדרבנן אין אב לגר וקאמר דהא שני אחין תאומים כו' וכן כל שאר שיש בו צד אב מותר לכתחלה אחות האב מן האם ואחות האם מן האב ואחותו מן האב ואע"ג דבברייתא שם כולן אסורין כבר אוקמוה כר"א משום דאחות האב אסור לב"נ אליביה אבל לר"ע ורבנן כל שיש בו צד האב מותר לגמרי וכ"כ הרמב"ן ורשב"א אבל אחות האם מן האם אסור לגר מד"ס אע"ג דמותר לב"נ מדקאמר אין אב לעובד כוכבים כו' משמע דאם יש לו וכן באחין מן האם דאסור כנ"ל וכן צד האב שמצד אישות מותר אפי' אשת אב לד"ה רק אחיו מאמו כנ"ל וכמו בקורבי עצמו וכמש"ש מאי לאו כו' לא כו' ולא קאי רק אאשת אחיו לבד דלא בפי' הראב"ד שקאי אכל האסורין מאישות דהא חשיב שם אשת אחי אביו והיא ודאי אפי' נשאה כשהוא גר. רמב"ן. ועוד חילוק בין ברייתא לרבנן דלהברייתא אחות אם מן האם יוציא אבל לרבנן יקיים כמו אחות אב מן האב לר"מ דאינו אלא משום אחלופי וה"ה לאחות האם מן האם לר"ע ורבנן וכ"ש באשת אחיו מאמו זהו שיטת הרמב"ם וז"ש אם היה נשוי כו' לשאר כו':
(ליקוט) עמש"ש והכלל להרמב"ם לב"נ אסור אמו ואחותו מאמו ואשת אביו ושאר מותר לגמרי וכרבנן דר"מ. ובגר צד אביו מותר לגמרי בין שמצד עצמו בין מצד אישות הלכך מותר אף באשת אב ובזה קל מעובד כוכבים אבל בזה חמור ממנו שכל מצד האם אסור לו בין מצד עצמו או מצד אישות הלכך אסור באמו ואחות אמו מן האם זהו מצד עצמו ומצד אשתו אסור אחות אשתו מאמה ובת אשתו ובת בתה וחמותו ואם חמותו וכמ"ש בס"ה הנושא כו' וה"ה כו' וה"ה להנך וכמ"ש בתוס' ורמב"ן ומצד אישות אסור באשת אחיו מאמו כולם ט' עריות. ושיטת הרמב"ן בגר כדברי הרמב"ם אלא בעובד כוכבים כתב דלד"ה אסור בכל העריות מצד אם ומותר מצד אב ומצד אישות ל"ל כלל רק אותן שפרטן אחות האב מן האם לר"א ואשת אב לר"ע אלא דלר"מ אליבא דר"ע אין אסור קרובי אם אלא מיתת ב"ד ולר"א ורבנן אף חייבי כריתות. ושיטה אחרת לרש"י וע' בדברי הרמב"ן (ע"כ):
beur_hagra.en:
How, etc. In chapter 9 of Hilchos Melachim, Rambam writes that six forbidden relations apply to a ben Noach: his mother, his father's wife, a married woman, his maternal sister, a male, and an animal. This is derived from the verse, "Therefore a man shall leave his father," meaning his father's wife, "and his mother," literally; "and shall cleave," excluding a male; "to his wife," excluding another man's wife; "and they shall become one flesh," excluding an animal. It is also stated, "She is indeed my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother, and she became my wife." These are the words of R' Akiva in Sanhedrin, daf 55a. Yet according to R' Akiva his sister is permitted, as stated there on daf 55b; see Rashi there, s.v. "come and hear," etc. Rambam, however, rules like the Sages on daf 57b and like the Toras Kohanim according to R' Yishmael: "Every forbidden relation," etc. The text appears not to read "many," but rather: there are relations for which a Jewish beit din does not execute, etc., namely those explained in the continuation, including his sister and a betrothed maiden. The matter of a betrothed maiden requires study. His sister is derived from "Therefore he shall leave," etc. According to R' Akiva the verse must be read less literally, while the Sages interpret it according to its plain meaning. In Toras Kohanim, Parashas Kedoshim, it is taught regarding "it is a disgraceful act": perhaps you will say that Kayin married his sister; Scripture therefore calls it an act of kindness, for at the beginning of the world it was permitted only because the world could not otherwise be established. This accords with Sanhedrin, daf 55b, "Come and hear, why," etc., and not with the Gemara's rejection there, nor with Rashi's explanation on daf 57b. Ramban likewise writes this, except that he holds that according to the Sages all maternal relatives are forbidden. The only dispute between Ramban and Rambam is therefore concerning the mother's sister through the mother, as explained by Ramban. There are twenty-two forbidden relations in all: four not based on kinship, namely a male, an animal, a married woman, and a niddah. All apply to a non-Jew except niddah. Eighteen are based on kinship, corresponding to the fifteen women and six forbidden relations listed in the first chapter of Yevamos, with the wife of one's brother counted in three forms and one's sister in two forms. Seven are one's own relatives, seven are relatives through one's wife, and four are wives of relatives whose husbands create the prohibition. For a ben Noach, the seven relatives through one's wife are all permitted because marital kinship does not create such relationships for non-Jews. Likewise, the four wives of relatives are all permitted except the father's wife, which R' Akiva derives from the verse, whereas according to R' Eliezer all are permitted. Of the seven direct blood relatives, those related through the father are all permitted, as stated in Yevamos, chapter 11, daf 98a, because a non-Jew has no halachic paternal relationship. Therefore the Gemara on daf 58b states that a non-Jew may marry his daughter, and all the more so his son's daughter and daughter's daughter. The same applies to the father's sister according to R' Akiva, whereas R' Eliezer derives a prohibition from the verse. Ramban nevertheless holds that the mother's sister is forbidden even according to R' Akiva, because the word "saying" extends the prohibition to maternal relatives. Rambam, however, holds that even according to the Sages only the mother and maternal sister, which are explicitly stated, are forbidden, as in the view of R' Meir according to R' Akiva. R' Meir and the Sages disagree only concerning his sister and the interpretation of the verse. The Gemara on daf 57b asks, "Does R' Meir hold," etc. Ramban explains that the question concerns only the latter clause, which says that a ben Noach is not warned, etc., while here the Baraisa includes his sister. It does not ask from the father's wife because the Sages did not decree other paternal relatives upon converts. This differs from Rashi's explanation there. Proof is that the Gemara challenges specifically according to R' Meir; according to Rashi the same difficulty would apply to the Sages, who do not disagree on that point. It answers that one source follows R' Meir, etc., and the Baraisa likewise cannot accord with the Sages except concerning the sister. In the dispute of R' Eliezer ben Yaakov and R' Shimon in Yevamos, daf 97b, Rambam rules like Rav Acha bar Yaakov and the first version, unlike the Rif. His reason is the statement on daf 98a: "This that the Sages said," etc., which implies that even rabbinically a convert has no paternal relationship. The Gemara says that twin brothers, etc., and therefore any kinship containing a paternal side is permitted l'chatchila: the father's sister through the mother, the mother's sister through the father, and a paternal sister. Although the Baraisa there forbids all of these, it has already been established according to R' Eliezer, who holds the father's sister is forbidden to a ben Noach. According to R' Akiva and the Sages, any relation containing a paternal side is entirely permitted. Ramban and Rashba likewise write this. A mother's sister through the mother, however, is rabbinically forbidden to a convert even though she is permitted to a ben Noach, because the Gemara's statement that a non-Jew has no father implies that maternal kinship does exist. The same applies to maternal brothers. Likewise, a paternal relationship created through marriage is permitted, even the father's wife according to all opinions, except for the wife of his maternal brother, as explained. The Gemara's statement, "What, is it not," etc., concerns only the wife of his brother, unlike the Ra'avad's explanation that it applies to all relations created through marriage. For the Gemara also counts the wife of his father's brother, who is certainly permitted even if that marriage occurred after conversion. Ramban. There is an additional distinction between the Baraisa and the Sages: according to the Baraisa, the mother's sister through the mother must be divorced, whereas according to the Sages he may retain her, like the father's sister through the father according to R' Meir, because the prohibition is only to prevent confusion. The same applies to the mother's sister through the mother according to R' Akiva and the Sages, and all the more so to the wife of his maternal brother. This is Rambam's approach, and this is the meaning of his words, "If he was married," etc., regarding the other relations, etc.
(Likkut) See what is written there. The general rule according to Rambam is as follows: for a ben Noach, his mother, maternal sister, and father's wife are forbidden, while all other relatives are entirely permitted, in accordance with the Sages who disagree with R' Meir. For a convert, paternal relationships are entirely permitted, whether direct blood relatives or relatives through marriage. He may therefore even marry his father's former wife, and in this respect a convert is more lenient than a non-Jew. On the other hand, every maternal relationship is forbidden to a convert, whether through direct blood relationship or through marriage. Thus, among his own relatives he is forbidden to his mother and his mother's sister through the mother. Among his wife's relatives he is forbidden to his wife's maternal sister, his wife's daughter and granddaughter, his mother-in-law, and his wife's maternal grandmother, as written in seif 5, "one who marries," etc.; the same applies to the corresponding cases, as Tosafos and Ramban write. Through marriage he is also forbidden to the wife of his maternal brother. These are nine forbidden relations in all. Ramban's approach regarding a convert agrees with Rambam, but regarding a non-Jew he holds that according to all opinions all maternal relatives are forbidden and all paternal relatives are permitted. Relations created through marriage do not apply at all except those explicitly specified: the father's sister through the mother according to R' Eliezer, and the father's wife according to R' Akiva. According to R' Meir in accordance with R' Akiva, only maternal relations punishable by death are forbidden, whereas according to R' Eliezer and the Sages even those punishable by karet are forbidden. Rashi has another approach; see Ramban's discussion. End.

mechaber.he: עובד כוכבים אסור בשאר האם אחר שנתגייר מדברי סופרים ומותר בשאר האב אע"פ שיודע בודאי שזה שארו מאביו כגון תאומים שדבר ברור הוא שאביו של זה הוא אביו של זה אף על פי כן לא גזרו על שאר אביו לפיכך נושא הגר אשת אחיו מאביו ואשת אחי אביו ואשת אביו ואשת בנו אף על פי שנשאת לאחיו או לאחי אביו או לבנו אחר שנתגיירו וכן אחות אמו מאביה ואחותו מאביו ובתו שנתגיירו מותרות לו (ויש אוסרים באשת אביו) (טור בה"ג) אבל אינו נושא לא אחותו מאמו ולא אחות אמו מאמה ולא אשת אחיו מאמו שנשאה אחיו מאמו אחר שנתגיירה אבל אם נשאה אחיו כשהיה עובד כוכבים הרי זה מותרת לו:
mechaber.en: A gentile is forbidden in his mother's other relatives after he converted by rabbinic decree; and he is permitted in his father's other relatives even though he knows certainly that this is his father's relative — such as twins, for it is a clear matter that this one's father is that one's father; even so they did not decree on his father's other relatives; therefore a convert may marry his father's brother's wife, his father's brother's wife, his father's wife, and his son's wife — even though she married his brother or his father's brother or his son after they converted; and likewise his mother's sister from her father, his sister from his father, and his daughter who converted are permitted to him: {Rama: (And some forbid his father's wife) (Tur in Beit HaGadol).} But he may not marry neither his maternal sister nor his mother's sister from her mother, nor his maternal brother's wife who married his maternal brother after she converted; but if his brother married her when he was still a gentile — behold she is permitted to him.

siftei_kohen.he:
עובד כוכבים אסור בשאר האם כו'. כלומר דאם לא היה נשוי כבר בשאר האם ונתגייר אסור לישא בכל שאר האם וכמו שיתבאר וכ' העט"ז בזו נ"ל שאפילו אם נשא יוציא כיון שנשא באיסור דיהדות חמיר טפי ע"כ וע"ל סעיף ה':
ויש אוסרים באשת אביו. ומדברי התוס' והרא"ש נראה שיש להחמיר גם באחות אביו כמ"ד שאסור לבני נח וכ"פ הב"ח כדברי שניהם:
אבל אם נשאה אחיו כשהיה עובד כוכבים ה"ז מותרת. שאינה אשת אחיו שלא היה לו קדושין בה כיון שנשאה בגיותו:
siftei_kohen.en:
A non-Jew is forbidden to maternal relatives, etc. Meaning, if he was not already married to a maternal relative and then converted, he is forbidden to marry any maternal relative, as will be explained. The Atteres Zahav writes: In this case it appears to me that even if he married her, he must divorce her, since he married her in violation of Jewish law, which is more stringent. See below, seif 5.
Some prohibit his father's wife. From Tosafos and the Rosh it appears that one should also be stringent regarding his father's sister, in accordance with the opinion that descendants of Noah are forbidden to her. The Bach rules stringently in accordance with both views.
But if his brother married her while he was a non-Jew, she is permitted. She is not considered his brother's wife, because his brother's marriage did not create kiddushin while he was a non-Jew.

baer_heitev.he:
באשת. ומדברי התוספות והרא"ש נראה שיש להחמיר גם באחות אביו כמ"ד שאסור לבני נח וכ"פ הב"ח עכ"ל הש"ך:
מותרת. שאינה אשת אחיו שלא היה לו קידושין בה כיון שנשאה בגיותו וכתב הלבוש דבשאר האם נ"ל שאפילו נשא יוציא כיון שנשא באיסור דיהדות חמיר מפי:
baer_heitev.en:
Concerning the wife of, etc. From Tosafot and Rosh it appears that one should likewise be stringent concerning his father's sister, in accordance with the opinion that this relation is forbidden to Noahides. Bach likewise ruled this way. These are the words of Siftei Kohen.
She is permitted. She is not considered his brother's wife, for his brother's marriage to her did not take effect according to Jewish law when he married her as a non-Jew. Levush writes that in the case of a maternal relative, it appears to him that even if he married her, he must divorce her, since the marriage was contracted in violation of a prohibition and Jewish law is more stringent.

beer_hagolah.he:
שם ומהא דציינתיו לעיל:
מימרא דרבא שם דף צ"ח ע"א דאפקורי אפקריה רחמנא לזרעי':
שם וכמ"ש ה"ה שם דהא דמוקים לה שם בנסבה כשהוא כותי קאי אהא דמשמע אפילו אחיו מאמו וכן הסכים הרמב"ן והרשב"א:
שם והא דאיתא שם ע"ב הנך דאמור רבנן יקיים לכתחלה לא יכנוס לא אמרו אליבא דרבי עקיבא כיון דלא מצינו להם שאר האב כלל:
שם וכן הסכימו הרמב"ן והרשב"א שהרי הכותי מותר בבתו:
שם מברייתא וגמרא שם ע"ב:
beer_hagolah.en:
There, and from what I cited above.
Rava's statement there, Yevamot 98a, that the Torah rendered his offspring ownerless.
There, as Maggid Mishneh explains, that the Gemara's case of marriage while still a non-Jew refers to the implication concerning even a maternal brother. Ramban and Rashba agreed.
There. The Gemara's rule that in relationships the Sages said he may retain but should not initially marry was not stated according to Rabbi Akiva, because paternal kinship is not recognized for them at all.
There, and Ramban and Rashba likewise agreed, since a non-Jew is permitted to his daughter.
There, from the baraita and Gemara, 98b.

beur_hagra.he:
עובד כוכבים אסור כו'. כמ"ש רבא שם הא דאמור רבנן כו' ובין בקורבה שמצד עצמו ובין שמצד אשת הקרוב וכמש"ו:
אע"פ כו' כגון כו'. כראב"י וכלישנא קמא:
לפיכך כו'. בברייתא שם:
וכן אחות כו'. דלא כברייתא אלא כרבנן כנ"ל:
ויש אוסרים כו'. כפירש"י הנ"ל דגם מאשת אב פריך ומשני הא ר"מ כו' ועתוס' דיבמות שם ד"ה אשת אביו כו' ומיהו כו' וכ"כ הטור וטוב להחמיר כדברי שניהם ובכ"ז אין חילוק בין הורתו שלא בקדושה ולידתו בקדושה או הורתו ולידתו שלא בקדושה ובן א' הורתו שלא בקדושה כו' כן הסכים הרמב"ן וכן סתם הרמב"ם וש"ע ועתוס' שם ד"ה נשא כו':
(ליקוט) ויש אוסרים בא"א. הוא מדברי הטור וכמש"ש אבל הרב לא עיין כאן דהטור פליג הרבה על הרמב"ם דלדידיה שפסק גם כר"א אסור גם באחותו ואחות אב ואחות האם מן האב כמ"ש בברייתא דשם ואין קולא בצד אב אלא מצד אישות כגון אשת אחיו מאביו ובן בדידה אחות אשה הגיורת מאב כמ"ש תוס' וכנ"ל ועוד דאחותו ואחות אביו ואחות אמו מן האם יוציא כמש"ש וכן באשת אביו יוציא שהוא פסק כדברי שניהם ועוד דפסק כר"ש דמן האב ומן האם אסור כמו מן האם לבד דלא כהרמב"ם שכתב שני אחין תאומים כו' (ע"כ):
אבל כו'. דכל שמצד אם לבד אסור כמו שאסור אשת אחיו מאמו וכנ"ל ומ"מ נראה דאחותו אף מן האב ואם אסור דהא לב"נ אסורה דהא ילפינן מדכתיב וגם אמנה כו' אך כו':
beur_hagra.en:
A non-Jew is forbidden, etc. As Rava states there: “That which the Sages said,” etc. This applies both to his own relatives and to relatives connected through the wife of a relative, as the Mechaber proceeds to explain.
From the mother. As stated in seif 7: “A man is permitted,” etc. These are Rambam's words. See Tosafos there, s.v. “A woman,” etc.; “Or perhaps,” etc. Rosh rules likewise. This is certainly so according to Rambam's approach, under which even one's own paternal relatives are permitted initially, as explained above.
Therefore, etc. This is stated in the baraisa there.
And likewise a sister, etc. This does not follow the baraisa, but rather the Sages, as explained above.
**
(Collection) And some forbid regarding a brother's wife.** This is from the words of the Tur, and as written there; but the Rav did not examine carefully here, for the Tur disputes the Rambam a great deal — for according to him, who also ruled like Rabbi Eliezer, it is forbidden also with his sister, and the father's sister, and the mother's sister from the father, as written in the baraita there; and there is no kula on the father's side except from the aspect of marriage, such as the wife of his brother from his father; and likewise regarding her — the sister of a convert-woman from the father, as Tosafot wrote, and as it appears to me. And further: his sister, and his father's sister, and his mother's sister from the mother — he must divorce, as written there; and likewise with his father's wife he must divorce, for he ruled according to both of them. And further: he ruled like Rabbi Shimon that from the father and from the mother it is forbidden like from the mother alone — unlike the Rambam who wrote “two twin brothers” etc. (end of quote).
And if he does not wish, etc. This follows from the statement there: If he married a woman and her daughter, he may retain one of them.

pitchei_teshuva.he: תאומים. עש"ך סק"ו דדוקא תאומים ועיין בתשובת נו"ב חלק אה"ע סוף סימן כ"ג שכתב דמדברי רש"י ביבמות דף צ"ח מבואר דלא כהש"ך אלא אפילו אינם תאומים אם היתה לידתם בקדושה איכא כרת ע"ש:
pitchei_teshuva.en: Twins. Shach note 36 — specifically twins; and see responsum Noda BiYehudah part Even HaEzer end of siman 23 who wrote that from Rashi\'s words in Yevamot 98 it is clear — not like Shach, but even if they are not twins, if their birth was in holiness there is karet — see there.

mechaber.he: שני אחים תאומים שהיתה הורתן שלא בקדושה ולידתן בקדושה חייבים משום אשת אחיו אבל לא חולצין ולא מיבמין:
mechaber.en: Two twin brothers whose conception was not in sanctity but whose birth was in sanctity — they are liable for a brother's wife, but neither perform chalitzah nor yibbum.

siftei_kohen.he:
חייבים משום אשת אח. דעת הב"י דאפי' אינן תאומים כיון שלידתן בקדושה חייבים משום אשת אח וכן דעת הב"ח וצ"ע דמדברי המחבר) משמע להדיא דדוקא תאומים וכן משמע בעט"ז) וכן משמע להדיא ברמב"ם והרב המגיד ס"פ ד' מהל' איסורי ביאה ע"ש:
אבל לא חולצין כו'. שמן התורה אינם אחים אלא מן האם ולא מן האב אע"פ שהן תאומים הרי נזרעו שלא בקדושה ואין כאן אבות ולענין חליצה ויבום אחין מן האב בעינן כמו שנתבאר בא"ע סי' קנ"ו אבל אם היתה הורתן ולידתן בקדושה הרי הן כישראל גמור לכל דבר וכ"כ הטור ופשוט הוא:
siftei_kohen.en:
They are liable because of a brother's wife. The Beis Yosef maintains that even if they are not twins, since they were born in sanctity they are liable for the prohibition of a brother's wife. This is also the view of the Bach. This requires study, for the Mechaber's words clearly imply that this applies specifically to twins. The Atteres Zahav likewise implies this, and it is also explicit in the Rambam and the Maggid Mishneh at the end of chapter 4 of Hilchos Issurei Biah. See there.
But they do not perform chalitzah, etc. By Torah law they are brothers only through their mother and not through their father. Although they are twins, they were conceived outside sanctity, and there is no legally recognized paternity here. For chalitzah and yibbum, paternal brothers are required, as explained in Even HaEzer, siman 156. If both their conception and birth were in sanctity, however, they are fully Jewish in every respect. The Tur writes likewise, and this is obvious.

baer_heitev.he: חולצין. שמן התורה אינם אלא אחים מן האם ולענין חליצה ויבום אחים מן האב בעינן כמ"ש בא"ע סימן קנ"ו:
baer_heitev.en: They perform chalitzah. According to the Torah, they are considered brothers only through their mother, whereas chalitzah and yibbum require brothers through their father, as stated in Even HaEzer, siman 156.

mechaber.he: הנושא גיורת ובתה הגיורת או שתי אחיות מן האם יושב עם אחת מהן ומגרש השניה:
mechaber.en: One who marries a convert and her convert daughter, or two sisters from the mother — he sits with one of them and divorces the other.

siftei_kohen.he:
או שתי אחיות. גיורות מן האם. אבל אחיות גיורות מן האב נושא אפי' לכתחלה וכמו שנתבאר דלא נאסר בשאר האב:
ומגרש השניה. היינו שצריכה גט דהא קידושין תפסי לו בה שאינן קרובות דכל גיורת כקטנה שנולדה דמי כ"כ העט"ז:
siftei_kohen.en:
Or two sisters. Maternal sisters who converted. Paternal sisters who converted may be married even initially, as explained, because paternal kinship was not prohibited.
And he divorces the second. Meaning, she requires a get, for kiddushin takes effect with her, since they are not legally related, every female convert being regarded as a newborn child. Thus wrote the Atteres Zahav.

baer_heitev.he: ומגרש. דהא קידושין תפסי לו בה שאינן קרובות דכל גיורת כקטנה שנולדה דמי כ"כ הלבוש אבל אחיות גיורות מן האב נושא אפילו לכתחלה וכמו שנתבאר דלא נאסר בשאר האב. ש"ך:
baer_heitev.en: And he divorces her. Betrothal takes effect with her because they are not legally relatives, since every female convert is considered like a newborn child. Thus writes Levush. A man may, however, marry even ab initio a female convert who shares his father, as explained above, because paternal relatives were not prohibited. Thus writes Siftei Kohen.

beer_hagolah.he:
לשון הרמב"ם שם וכפי פירושו בברייתא שם דף צ"ח ע"ב:
מדין גיורת ובתה וכן כתבו התוספו' שם:
beer_hagolah.en:
The wording of Rambam there, according to his explanation of the baraita, Yevamot 98b.
From the law of a female convert and her daughter; Tosafot likewise writes this there.

beur_hagra.he: מן האם. כמ"ש בס"ז מותר לאדם כו' והן דברי הרמב"ם ועתוס' שם ד"ה אשה כו' או שמא כו' וכ"פ הרא"ש וכ"ש לשיטת הרמב"ם דאף בקרובי עצמו מצד האב מותר לכתחלה כנ"ל:
beur_hagra.en: From the mother. As stated in seif 7: “A man is permitted,” etc. These are Rambam's words. See Tosafos there, s.v. “A woman,” etc.; “Or perhaps,” etc. Rosh rules likewise. This is certainly so according to Rambam's approach, under which even one's own paternal relatives are permitted initially, as explained above.

mechaber.he: נשא גיורת ומתה מותר לישא אמה או בתה שלא גזרו אלא בחייהן:
mechaber.en: One who married a convert and she died — he is permitted to marry her mother or daughter, for they decreed only while they live.

siftei_kohen.he: מותר כו'.כיון דליכא לאחר מיתה אלא איסור כרת לא גזרו כיון שגם בחיים ליכא אלא גזירה ויש פוסקים דאפילו לאחר מיתה אסור וכן נראה דעת הטור להחמיר:
siftei_kohen.en: It is permitted, etc. Since after death there is only a prohibition punishable by kareis, the Sages did not decree, because even during her lifetime the prohibition is only rabbinic. Some authorities maintain that it remains forbidden even after death, and the Tur also appears to rule stringently.

baer_heitev.he: בחייהן. ויש פוסקים דאפילו לאחר מיתה אסור וכ"נ דעת הטור להחמיר. ש"ך:
baer_heitev.en: During their lifetimes. Some halachic authorities prohibit this even after their deaths, and Tur likewise appears to rule stringently. Thus writes Siftei Kohen.

beer_hagolah.en: There in the baraita, following Rabbi Akiva.

mechaber.he: מותר לאדם לישא שתי אחיות גיורות מן האב שלא גזרו משאר האב:
mechaber.en: It is permitted for a man to marry two convert sisters from the father, for they did not decree on the father's other relatives.

beer_hagolah.he: רמב"ם שם וכרבי עקיבא וכמ"ש לעיל:
beer_hagolah.en: Rambam there, following Rabbi Akiva, as explained above.

mechaber.he: השניות כולן לא גזרו עליהן בגרים לפיכך מותר הגר לישא אם אמו ונושא אדם גיורת ואם אמה או בת בת בתה וכן בשאר השניות:
mechaber.en: The secondary forbidden relations — they did not decree upon them for converts; therefore a convert is permitted to marry his mother's mother; and a man may marry a convert and her mother, or daughter, or daughter's daughter's daughter; and likewise with the other secondary relations.

siftei_kohen.he:
השניות כו'. ע' בא"ע סט"ו איזה ערוה דאורייתא ואיזה שניות דרבנן:
או בת בת בתה. כ"ה בספרי המחבר ובספרי הרמב"ם. ובעט"ז הגיה או בת בתה משום דקשיא ליה דברישא נקיט אם אמה לפיכך כתב ונושא אדם גיורת ואם אמה או בת בתה עכ"ל והוא טעות דאם אמה ובת בתה אסורות מדאוריי' כמו שנתבאר בא"ע סי' ט"ו סי"ג וט"ו ומקרא מלח דבר הכתוב את בת בתה ואת בת בנה לא תקח אלא הדבר פשוט דברישא צ"ל נושא אדם גיורת ואם אם אמה וכן הביא מדרישה לשון הרמב"ם וזה ברור:
siftei_kohen.en:
The secondary forbidden relations, etc. See Even HaEzer, siman 15, regarding which relations are forbidden by Torah law and which are rabbinic secondary relations.
Or her great-granddaughter through her daughter. This is the reading in the editions of the Mechaber and the Rambam. The Atteres Zahav emended it to read, 'or her granddaughter through her daughter,' because he found it difficult that the first clause mentions her mother's mother. He therefore wrote: A man may marry a female convert together with her mother's mother or her daughter's daughter. End quote. This is an error, for her mother's mother and her daughter's daughter are forbidden by Torah law, as explained in Even HaEzer, siman 15, seifim 13 and 15, and Scripture explicitly states, 'You shall not take her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter.' Rather, it is obvious that the first clause should read: A man may marry a female convert together with her mother's mother's mother. The Derishah also cites the Rambam's wording this way. This is clear.

baer_heitev.he: ואם. כתב הש"ך דצ"ל אם אם אמה אבל אם אמה ובת בתה אסורות מדאורייתא ומקרא מלא הוא את בת בנה ואת בת בתה לא תקח וזה ברור עכ"ל:
baer_heitev.en: And if, etc. Siftei Kohen writes that the text must read, "her mother's mother." Her mother and her daughter's daughter, however, are forbidden according to the Torah, as the verse explicitly states, "You shall not take her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter." This is clear.

beer_hagolah.he: בעיא ונפשטא שם דף כ"ב ע"א:
beer_hagolah.en: An unresolved question that was resolved there, Yevamot 22a.

mechaber.he: גר שנתגייר ואשתו עמו צריכים לפרוש זה מזה ג' חדשים להבחין בין זרע שנזרע בקדושה לזרע שנזרע שלא בקדושה ואם אינו רוצה לקיימה אינה צריכה גט אלא יוצאה ממנו בלא גט (נ"י פ' נושאין על האנוסה):
mechaber.en: A convert who converted and his wife with him — they must separate from each other three months to distinguish between seed sown in sanctity and seed sown not in sanctity: {Rama: And if he does not wish to maintain her, she does not need a get but leaves him without a get (Nimmukei Yosef, chapter Nosein al haAnusah).}

pitchei_teshuva.he:
צריכים לפרוש. עיין בדגול מרבבה שכתב דאם היא זקינה אין צריך הפרשה ואף שהח"מ באה"ע סימן י"ג סק"ד נסתפק בזה היינו בנתגיירה היא ונשאת לאחר אבל בנתגיירו שניהם ונשארו יחד א"צ הפרשה ע"ש. עוד כתב שאחר שלשה חדשים כשמחזירה א"צ שבעה נקיים אם לא פרסה נדה בינתיים ואף שכתוב לעיל סוף סימן קצ"ב שמחזיר גרושתו צריכה ז"נ שאני התם שגירשה לחלוטין משא"כ הכא ע"ש:
אינו רוצה לקיימה. עיין בדגול מרבבה שכתב הא ודאי שאם רוצה לקיימה צריך חופה וקידושין בדת יהדות ולענין כתובתה עיין באה"ע סוף סימן ס"ז:
צריכים לפרוש. עיין בדגול מרבבה שכתב דאם היא זקינה אין צריך הפרשה ואף שהח"מ באה"ע סימן י"ג סק"ד נסתפק בזה היינו בנתגיירה היא ונשאת לאחר אבל בנתגיירו שניהם ונשארו יחד א"צ הפרשה ע"ש. עוד כתב שאחר שלשה חדשים כשמחזירה א"צ שבעה נקיים אם לא פרסה נדה בינתיים ואף שכתוב לעיל סוף סימן קצ"ב שמחזיר גרושתו צריכה ז"נ שאני התם שגירשה לחלוטין משא"כ הכא ע"ש:
אינו רוצה לקיימה. עיין בדגול מרבבה שכתב הא ודאי שאם רוצה לקיימה צריך חופה וקידושין בדת יהדות ולענין כתובתה עיין באה"ע סוף סימן ס"ז:
pitchei_teshuva.en:
They need to separate. See Dagul Merevavah who wrote that if she is elderly there is no need for separation; and even though Choshen Mishpat in EH siman 13 s.k. 4 was uncertain about this — that is when she converted and married another afterward; but if both converted and remained together — no separation is needed — see there. He also wrote that after three months when he takes her back he does not need seven clean days if she did not establish niddah in the interim; and even though it is written above at the end of siman 192 that one who takes back his divorcee needs seven clean days — there is different, for there he divorced her completely, unlike here — see there.
He does not want to maintain her. See Dagul Merevavah who wrote — behold certainly if he wants to maintain her he needs chuppah and kiddushin according to Jewish law; and regarding her ketubah see EH at the end of siman 67.
They need to separate. See Dagul Merevavah who wrote that if she is elderly there is no need for separation; and even though Choshen Mishpat in EH siman 13 s.k. 4 was uncertain about this — that is when she converted and married another afterward; but if both converted and remained together — no separation is needed — see there. He also wrote that after three months when he takes her back he does not need seven clean days if she did not establish niddah in the interim; and even though it is written above at the end of siman 192 that one who takes back his divorcee needs seven clean days — there is different, for there he divorced her completely, unlike here — see there.
Twins. Shach note 36 — specifically twins; and see responsum Noda BiYehudah part Even HaEzer end of siman 23 who wrote that from Rashi\'s words in Yevamot 98 it is clear — not like Shach, but even if they are not twins, if their birth was in holiness there is karet — see there.

mechaber.he: ולענין עדות אפי' אחים מן האם מעידים זה לזה דגר שנתגייר כקטן שנולד דמי:
mechaber.en: Regarding testimony — even brothers from the mother testify for each other, for a convert who converted is like a child just born.

siftei_kohen.he: מעידין זה לזה. וליכא למיחש דלמא אתי לאחלופי בישראל שהרי אין מקבלין עדות אלא בב"ד וסתם ב"ד בקיאין בדבר ועיין בח"מ סי' ל"ג סי"א ובד' האחרונים שם:
siftei_kohen.en: They may testify for one another. There is no concern that this will be confused with the law of Jews, because testimony is accepted only in beit din, and an ordinary beit din is knowledgeable in this matter. See Choshen Mishpat, siman 33, seif 11, and the later authorities there.

baer_heitev.he: עדות. עיין בח"מ סימן ל"ג סי"א מדינים אלו:
baer_heitev.en: Testimony. See Choshen Mishpat, siman 33, se'if 11, concerning these laws.

beer_hagolah.he: לשון הטור ממימרא דאמימר יבמות דף כ"ב ע"א ומשמע דרב נחמן שם כי שמע להא דאמימר שתיק ואודי ליה ולא חיישינן לאחלופי בישראל דאין מקבלין עדות אלא בבית דין והם בקיאין בדבר:
beer_hagolah.en: The wording of the Tur, from Ameimar's statement, Yevamot 22a. Rav Nachman remained silent when he heard Ameimar's ruling and thereby accepted it. We are not concerned that he will be confused with an ordinary Jew, because testimony is accepted only in beit din, whose judges are expert in the matter.

mechaber.he: לענין דין גר כשר לדון דיני ממונות והוא שתהא אמו מישראל אבל אם אין אמו מישראל פסול לדון את ישראל אבל לחבירו גר דן ולחליצה פסול אפילו לחליצת גרים עד שיהא אביו ואמו מישראל:
mechaber.en: Regarding the law of a convert — he is fit to judge monetary cases if his mother is from Israel; but if his mother is not from Israel, he is disqualified to judge Israelites; but for his fellow convert he judges; and for chalitzah he is disqualified — even for chalitzah of converts — until his father and mother are from Israel.

siftei_kohen.he:
אמו כו'. ובחשן משפט ר"ס ז' כתב הרב דהוא הדין אביו מישראל ועיין בסמ"ע שם:
פסול לדון את ישראל. אפילו דיני ממונות ודוקא על ידי כפיה אבל אם מקבלו עליו לדין מותר כן כתבו הרא"ש וטור וכן כתב העט"ז:
ולחליצה כו'. כלומר להיות דיין בחליצה:
עד שיהא אביו ואמו מישראל. ובא"ע סימן קס"ט ס"ב נתבאר די"א דאם אביו מישראל כשר:
siftei_kohen.en:
His mother, etc. In Choshen Mishpat at the beginning of siman 7, the Rama writes that the same applies if his father is Jewish. See the Sema there.
He is disqualified from judging a Jew. This applies even to monetary law, and specifically when exercising coercive authority. If the litigant accepts him as a judge, however, it is permitted. Thus wrote the Rosh and the Tur, and likewise the Atteres Zahav.
And for chalitzah, etc. Meaning, to serve as a judge on a chalitzah panel.
Unless both his father and mother are Jewish. In Even HaEzer, siman 169, seif 2, it is explained that some say he is qualified if his father is Jewish.

baer_heitev.he:
אמו. ובח"מ ר"ס ז' כתב הרב דה"ה אביו מישראל וע"ש בסמ"ע:
לדון. אפילו דיני ממונות ודוקא ע"י כפי' אבל אם מקבלו עליו לדון מותר כ"כ הרא"ש והטור וכ"פ הלבוש:
ולחליצה. פי' להיות דיין בחליצה ובא"ע סימן קס"ט ס"ב נתבאר די"א דאם אביו מישראל כשר ע"ש:
baer_heitev.en:
His mother. At the beginning of Choshen Mishpat, siman 7, Rema writes that the same applies if his father is Jewish. See Sema there.
To adjudicate. This applies even to monetary law, but only when he would adjudicate coercively. If the litigants accept him as their judge, it is permitted. Thus wrote Rosh and Tur, and Levush likewise ruled.
And for chalitzah. This means serving as a judge for chalitzah. Even HaEzer, siman 169, se'if 2, explains that some authorities hold that if his father is Jewish, he is eligible. See there.

beer_hagolah.he: שם ממימרא דרבא שם דף ק"ב ע"ב וכמ"ש התוס' שם דף מ"ה ע"ב וכ"כ הרא"ש שם בפסקיו והרי"ף בפ"ק דסנהד' והרמב"ם בפי"א מהל' סנהדרין:
beer_hagolah.en: There, from Rava's statement, Yevamot 102b, as Tosafot writes there, 45b. The Rosh writes likewise in his rulings, as do the Rif in the first chapter of Sanhedrin and Rambam in chapter 11 of Hilchot Sanhedrin.

beur_hagra.he: ואם אינו רוצה כו'. ממש"ש נשא אשה ובתה כונס אחת:
beur_hagra.en: And if he does not wish, etc. This follows from the statement there: If he married a woman and her daughter, he may retain one of them.

pitchei_teshuva.he:
ולחליצה פסול. ועיין בתשובת נחלה ליהושע סימן כ"ז אם גר כשר להצטרף לענין חליצה או כל החמשה צריכים שיהיו כשרים ע"ש:
ולחליצה פסול. ועיין בתשובת נחלה ליהושע סימן כ"ז אם גר כשר להצטרף לענין חליצה או כל החמשה צריכים שיהיו כשרים ע"ש:
pitchei_teshuva.en:
and a flaw. See the answer to Joshua as a sign of “If a kosher person is to join the issue of a partition or all the exaggeration should be kosher:
and a flaw. See the answer to Joshua as a sign of “If a kosher person is to join the issue of a partition or all the exaggeration should be kosher:

rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.he: (סי' רס"ט סעיף י"א) פסול לדון את ישראל. כתב הרמב"ם (פ"ד מהל' מלכים ה"ד) אין מעמידים מלך מקהל גרים עד שתהיה אמו מישראל ולא למלכות בלבד אלא לכל שררות שבישראל וכו' ואפי' ממונה על אמת המים שמחלקים ממנו לשדות ואצ"ל דיין או נשיא וכו' אפי' אחר כמה דורות. הועתק במהריק"ש וע' ?בהג"מ:
rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.en: (Siman 269 seif 11) Disqualified to judge Israel. Rambam wrote (chapter 4 of Hilchot Melachim halachah 4): We do not appoint a king from the congregation of converts until his mother is from Israel; and not only for kingship but for any authority in Israel, etc.; and even one appointed over the water distribution that they divide from it to the fields — and all the more so a judge or nasi, etc., even after many generations. Copied in Maharikash — see Hagahot Maimoniyot.
